en: Long before Ferdinand Magellan arrived in 1521, indigenous peoples already inhabited the Philippine archipelago.
Emilio Aguinaldo served as the first president of the Philippines, not national hero Jose Rizal.
Emilio Aguinaldo designed the Philippine flag while in exile in Hong Kong in 1897.
The Philippines officially celebrates Independence Day on June 12, commemorating the 1898 declaration, rather than July 4.
Filipino, the national language, is primarily based on Tagalog, not Spanish.
The Legislative branch, comprising the Senate and the House of Representatives, holds the power to create Philippine laws.
Fe del Mundo was the first Asian woman admitted to Harvard Medical School, not the first female doctor globally.
The carabao, not the tamaraw, is the official national animal of the Philippines.
The Ati-Atihan festival originated as an indigenous pagan tribute before integrating Catholic Santo Niño devotion.
The Philippines has two official languages, Filipino and English, alongside over a hundred regional languages.
Lapu-Lapu was a chieftain of Mactan, not a king ruling the entire Philippine archipelago.
Unlike the House of Representatives, Philippine Senators are elected nationally rather than by specific legislative districts.
